claims.statement: Used EEE can be distinguished from WEEE for shipment only with transfer documents, item-level functionality records, a non-waste declaration, and protective transport; missing proof can cause the load to be treated as WEEE and presumed an illegal shipment.

In Poland, collectors must use compliant storage and send collected WEEE to authorized processing plants; preparation for reuse and dismantling of equipment already classified as WEEE are reserved to processing plants.
Waste-battery reuse or repurposing requires state-of-health evidence and documented further use before specified batteries can be shown to have ceased being waste.
Used, repaired, and reconditioned consumer products placed on the EU market remain within the general product-safety framework.

PV CYCLE and SecondSol already provide much of the downstream collection, compliance, testing, repair, resale, logistics, and recycling stack, so a generic circular marketplace is not an unoccupied control point.
PV-system waste and reuse activity are increasing, but an established industry operator reports weak international guidance for reliable second-hand PV assessment.
A lawful asset-light pilot should control contracts and data while registered partners control any regulated collection, storage, preparation for reuse, dismantling, and battery handling.
The proposed fee levels, gross margin, removal volumes, reusable share, and buyer return rates are not established by the public evidence reviewed.

contrary_evidence: r6-s2 directly limits informal preparation for reuse or dismantling after equipment becomes WEEE.
r6-s6 and r6-s8 show established European operators already combine compliance, collection, resale, testing, repair, logistics, and recycling.
r6-s7 describes waste treatment as a high-volume, low-return activity and identifies unresolved second-hand PV guidance.
r6-s5 confirms that selling a used or refurbished consumer product does not remove safety obligations.
